entries.name: Enkutatash
entries.capsule: Ethiopian New Year, Meskerem 1, marked in Minnesota with a public community celebration, music, food and traditional dress.
entries.dateRule: Meskerem 1 on the Ethiopian calendar: September 11, or September 12 in the Gregorian year before a Gregorian leap year. Minnesota community celebrations are often held on a nearby weekend.

entries.whatItMarks: The start of the Ethiopian year.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The Ethiopian Community in Minnesota held a free public celebration at Highland Park Pavilion, St. Paul, on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026, 2 to 7 p.m., with food, music, dance and traditional dress. In 2022, the fourth annual Ethiopian Fest of Minnesota (Sept. 4, Eden Prairie High School stadium, with concerts in West St. Paul) was tied to the coming New Year; no later edition was confirmed.

entries.name: Meskel
entries.capsule: Orthodox feast of the Finding of the True Cross, marked with a bonfire (Demera) the evening before or on a nearby Sunday.
entries.dateRule: Meskerem 17 on the Ethiopian calendar: September 27, or September 28 when Enkutatash falls on September 12. Office Holidays lists Sept. 27 for 2027; the calendar rule gives Sept. 28.
